lesson.subtitle: Lesson 14 -- The Study Group
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Mauricio | Lesson 14 -- The Study Group

listenings.text: OK, everyone, it is nine o'clock, and we have to present the case at eight tomorrow morning. Let's divide up the work. Kenji, you know the numbers, so you have to check the figures. Ana, can you write a draft of the slides? I will present the problem, and someone else has to present the recommendation. We don't have to finish everything tonight, but we must agree on the recommendation before we leave this room. Tomorrow we meet at seven to rehearse. Twenty minutes, not more. And please, everybody contributes. Nobody has to be perfect.

In my study group, I was the quiet one for two days. I thought, I don't have to speak, the others are better at this. On Wednesday, a woman from Singapore looked at me and said, you have to tell us what you think, you are the only banker here. So I volunteered to present the numbers the next morning. I rehearsed three times in my hotel room. The presentation was not perfect, but after that, the group asked for my opinion on every case. My advice is simple. You don't have to speak a lot. But you must speak early.

paras: In most executive programs, the study group is where the real work happens. You do not choose your group. It is assigned on the first day, and it usually has five or six people from different countries and industries. Every evening, the group has to prepare one case for the next morning.

The first rule is simple: everybody has to contribute. You don't have to be the best speaker in the group, but you must say something in every meeting. If you stay quiet for two days, the others will stop asking for your opinion.

Most groups divide up the work. One person checks the numbers, one person writes a draft of the slides, and one person presents. Good groups take turns, so the same person does not present every time. You don't have to present on the first day, but you should volunteer before Wednesday.

Before the presentation, the group has to rehearse at least once, and everybody must be on the same page about the recommendation. At the end, one person wraps up in thirty seconds. Past participants all say the same thing: the group is not a test of your English. It is the place where you can practice it.
